Oh my god we have a race!!

What I take home from this race:
- We knew that the advantage of being in front was big, it's probably bigger than we though. The Mercs never seemed able to overcome the Ferrari, even though the Ferrari was running with an old engine, pre-upgrade
- When starting aid is eliminated after the summer break, there is a chance to see some interesting mix-ups during races
- God, how much I hate Force India. First they veto Manor's return on inexistent safety concern, then they are the ones whose car collapses during the race in an incredibly dangerous manner
- Still cannot make up my mind about Kimi. What should Ferrari do? He was really good today!

I think it's time for Ferrari to groom the next generation and bring Bottas on. I think Kimi has a couple good years left but he's been too erratic this year and further off Seb's pace than Ferrari would like.

Regarding the Mercs, I think this race shows that they really, really do not like dirty air, since Nico couldn't make a dent at all after the safety car. Lewis had very good place in clean air. Another takeaway is that Nico can be somewhat of a shrinking violet at times. This was a perfect opportunity to blow the drivers championship wide open and he got the worst of all possible outcomes.

And congrats to McLaren putting two cars in the points. Maybe they have taken a significant step forward (at least in race pace).

Kimi is still a great rear gunner for Seb, and I reckon if he didn't have the MGU-K issues he would have held up Rosberg for much longer. He managed to do exactly what he needed before the safety car which was stick close to Seb and not let Rosberg overtake, and I think Ferrari are in a stronger position having a clear number one and two in the team on pace.

Nico is also getting way too much stick for his performance. He was beating Hamilton on pace for the first part of the race (bear in mind that Hamilton was in traffic however), and excluding his one mistake managed to stay out of trouble for the race which is what he needed to do. Compare that to Hamilton who was clearly ruffled by his start and drove stupid like pushing Bottas wide when Lewis was exiting the pits. If it was a different driver who wouldn't have conceded the position Lewis would be in a lot more shit atm.
Nico could have probably gotten ahead of Vettel if he'd been racing him and not Hamilton. If he hadn't insisted on getting the harder compound, he probably could have had a victory.

What an incredible race! Vettel wins, and always nice to see a new face on the podium. Hamilton had an absolute shocker. On his day is sublime but man. He can bin it and lose his cool far too easily sometimes. He's lucky his team mate can be an idiot as well, cutting across Ricciardo like that was a rookie mistake by Rosberg.

I think the Rosberg incident is an interesting one. I may be remembering things incorrectly but at Spa last year didn't Hamilton do the same thing and everyone said it was Rosberg's fault for not moving? Why is it different now?

I think the major difference is that Lewis and Nico were on the same team. Otherwise it's a racing incident. I think today's incident was also a racing incident but if you're Nico, you're running in second, Lewis is in 10th, you can get even on points in the championship... You don't throw that away by putting the squeeze on Ricciardo.

Honestly, I think he just didn't expect Ricciardo to be there. You saw how wide he ran, and his front wing was only over Rosberg's back wheel by a few millimetres. Call it a rookie mistake or his poor racing skills showing, but I really don't think it was that bad, it just had some pretty dire consequences.

You're right, it wasn't a huge mistake, but one with huge consequences.

I wouldn't compare Rosberg's move on Ricciardo here to that of him against Hamilton at Spa last year. To me a more similar incident would be Vettel on Narain Karthikeyan on the Malaysian Grand Prix 2012. There Vettel was lapping the HRT when he cut across Karthikeyan and sliced his rear tyres. When moving back onto the racing line Vettel had simply failed to leave enough room.

Today Rosberg did much the same thing. Ricciardo was basically straightening up his car for the run into turn 2 and Rosberg failed to give him sufficient room. Ricciardo had nowhere to go.

Ricciardo didn't have any right to the racing line though, and Rosberg just followed it. This is the same as what happened in Spa, Hamilton followed the line and Rosberg didn't move. I agree it should be a racing incident, but I think more fault lies on Ricciardo for not giving way than does on Rosberg for moving over. At another point in the race Hamilton ran very wide on pit exit, pushing Bottas wide. I didn't think that was particularly nice, but the fact that he didn't get a penalty shows that when you are in front, you are entitled to the racing line.

I'm not saying that Ricciardo was entitled to the racing line, but what I am saying is that there was no way he could have expected Rosberg to cut across in front of him like that. Who moved across and collided with who? Rosberg onto Ricciardo, just like Vettel moved across onto the racing line too early and clipped Karthikeyan. In both incidents the punctures could have been avoided had the drivers moving back onto the racing line not come across too early.

Also I agree with you on the Bottas incident, I'm guessing that it was just within the limit of what is tolerable without being penalized.
Yeah I see what you're saying, I just find it odd that everyone seemed to be (at least initially) all anti-Rosberg about the incident. Ricciardo must have a Mercedes magnet on him with his luck!

I think a lot of people are just disappointed he didn't capitalize on Hamilton having a bad day, and get back into the championship. I'm constantly hoping the Nico we saw in Austria turns up to every race!

Dan definitely was living up to his nickname today! Delighted for the fella, you could really tell Bianchi's death affected him greatly.

Yeah, I don’t think it was egregious... I just thought that discretion was the best part of valor there, even if it meant giving Ricciardo some room and even if Ricciardo should’ve backed out of the throttle. Whether Nico finished 2nd or 3rd, it would’ve been a huge coup for him because Lewis was more or less out of the points. As it stands, Nico went from potentially leading the WDC to somehow falling further behind. But it’s easy to dissect decisions that have to be made in a split second with limited information.
